text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Five civilians and ten policemen were injured in scuffles when around 200 people tried to block a major road in a Tirana suburb in a protest over land ownership.

- A representative from both of the main parties -- the ruling Democratic Party and opposition Socialists -- will distribute the voting papers for the October 20 local elections to minimise vote manipulation.
- Democratic Party members in the central electoral commission say the shortage of hotels in Tirana means only around 200 international observers can be accommodated during the elections.
- Socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis's victory in the Greek elections was evidence of the new trend in Europe away from nationalism, a newspaper commentary says.
- A Tirana prosecutor demanded jail terms of up to 25 years for nine senior figures of Albania's former communist regime, charged with political persecution while in office.
- Along with the current runway reconstruction at Rinasi airport outside Tirana, construction of a new terminal is planned for next year.
- A young Albanian left for the United States under police protection fearing a bloody vendetta from a feud with another family.

- Opposition Socialist leaders denied rumours of factions within the party which were reported to have developed after a major convention in August where sweeping changes were made to the party programme.
- The United States will send 25 observers for the forthcoming local elections.
- The government will distribute a second group of privatisation vouchers worth 60 billion leks from November 1.
- A newspaper commentary says the Democratic Party will achieve a greater victory in the October local elections than in the last general poll.
- Italy offered to provide 500 observers for the elections.
